clue.text: Daughter is in public events, not once showing the effects of alcohol and drugs?

definitions.text: showing the effects of alcohol and drugs?

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in family trees

indicators.note: not tells us the following word for former is removed from the public events

parts.note: exhibitions are public shows or displays
ex- means former, so once can be EX

explanation.surface: A daughter keeps attending public events, behaving under the influence like never before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' is the old prefix ex- (as in ex-wife), and 'not' takes it away from the shows; 'public events' looks like the setting but is the word being cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Drink and drugs lower restraint, so their effects show as a loss of inhibitions; the question mark admits a loose, plural sense.

clue.text: Mountain range close to Rabat in the end

parts.note: the Atlas Mountains run across Morocco

indicators.note: close to here means the closing letter of the word Rabat

explanation.surface: A traveller describes the Atlas mountains near Rabat, Morocco's capital, as they finally arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are idioms meaning finally, after a long wait or process.

clue.text: Woman's niece regularly employed in Italian city

indicators.note: employed in means the picked letters are put to work inside the city's name

parts.note: Verona is a city in northern Italy

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of niece, here the second and fourth

explanation.surface: A woman's niece has a regular job in an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of niece, IC, and 'employed in' sets them inside VERONA. The 's stands for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronica is a female given name, so the clue's woman is an example of someone so named.

clue.text: King of New York with a different mind-set

indicators.note: different asks for these letters to be made into something different, a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A New York monarch, or tycoon, with an unusual outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges KING + OF + NY + WITH + A.
explanation.definitionFit: A mind-set is a habitual mental outlook, the same idea as a characteristic mode of thought.

clue.text: She could get pulled in after palming a little money

indicators.note: palming means holding something hidden in the hand, so the earnings word encloses the other letters

parts.note: to pull in money is to earn or make it
M is a short form, a little version, of money

explanation.surface: A woman risks arrest after pocketing a small sum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'palming' puts A and M inside MADE. A madame runs a brothel, so 'She could get pulled in' (arrested) fits the surface too.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame is a title for a woman, also used for a brothel keeper, so she is a female figure.

clue.text: French film for all the family, one without sex getting close to completion

parts.note: U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for everyone
it is the pronoun used for a thing without sex

indicators.note: getting close to points to the closing letters of the following word

explanation.surface: A French family film, free of sex scenes, is almost finished.
explanation.walkthrough: IT is the neuter pronoun, for one without sex; 'getting close to' takes the last three letters of completion, ION. U is the British certificate for a film anyone may see.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruition is the realisation or fulfilment of a plan, synonymous with its being brought to an end.

clue.text: After work I want to hold that woman out of habit

indicators.note: to hold says the shuffled letters wrap round the pronoun
after work means once the letters have been worked over, reshaped into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
her is the pronoun for that woman

explanation.surface: After work, someone wants to embrace a woman, breaking a habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After work' rearranges I and want into INTAW before 'to hold' takes in the pronoun. The definition is a pun: a nun out of her habit would be naked.
explanation.definitionFit: A nun's habit is her robe, so being out of it humorously means naked, which is what this idiom means.

clue.text: Wild West lawman can be heard in the small room

indicators.note: can be heard says we want a word sounding like the lawman's surname

parts.note: Pat Garrett was the sheriff who shot Billy the Kid

explanation.surface: A famous sheriff's voice carries in a cramped room.
explanation.definitionFit: A garret is a small attic room at the top of a house.

clue.text: State dance tune

parts.note: Tennessee is a US state
the waltz is a ballroom dance

explanation.definitionFit: The Tennessee Waltz is a famous country song, popularised by Patti Page, so it is a melody.

clue.text: An element in Dublin knocked around with big rugby player

indicators.note: knocked around means battered out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a lock is a second-row forward in rugby

explanation.surface: Someone in Dublin gets roughed up alongside a hefty rugby forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked around' rearranges the city plus big; 'big' looks like it describes the player, but it is fodder. A lock is a second-row forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A building block is a basic component from which something is built, a fundamental part.

clue.text: A section of Florida Hospital is in a different part of America

definitions.text: is in a different part of America

indicators.note: A section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a Florida hospital is located somewhere else in the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across FlorIDA HOspital. The definition plays on Florida: the hidden state lies in another part of the US.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is a north-western state, far from Florida, so it lies elsewhere in the USA.

clue.text: University student breaks into applause as a type of release

indicators.note: breaks into means the letters force their way inside the applause word

parts.note: an ovation is a burst of applause
L is the learner plate letter, used for a student

explanation.surface: A student at university interrupts the clapping, a kind of emotional outpouring.
explanation.walkthrough: L comes from the learner plates on British cars; 'breaks into' sets U and L inside OVATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovulation is the release of an egg from the ovary.

clue.text: A group of people targeted and almost emptied high street bank

indicators.note: almost emptied means nearly all the inside letters go, leaving the outsides and one letter within

parts.note: to bank is to tilt, as a ship lists

explanation.surface: A high-street bank has nearly been cleared out by targeted thieves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost emptied' strips HIGH STREET to HIT, keeping its ends and one inner letter; LIST means bank, as an aircraft or ship leans.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit list names people marked for attack or killing, so they are the chosen victims.

clue.text: Shelter or else die in storm

indicators.note: in storm means the letters are tossed about as by bad weather

explanation.surface: Take cover in a storm, or perish.
explanation.definitionFit: The lee side is the side sheltered from the wind, so it offers protection from the weather.

clue.text: Radical lesbians in play areas for holidaymakers

indicators.note: in play means the letters are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: Militant lesbians appear in a stage drama.
explanation.definitionFit: The Balearic Islands, Majorca, Ibiza and others, are Mediterranean tourist destinations.

clue.text: Endless clichés in play

indicators.note: Endless means the word for clichés loses both its end letters

parts.note: platitudes are trite remarks, clichés

explanation.surface: A play stuffed with never-ending clichés.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' strips P and S from PLATITUDES.
explanation.definitionFit: Play here means freedom of movement or scope, as in slack in a rope.

clue.text: Artificial intelligence apparently explained?

parts.note: AI is shown nakedly placed inside the word laid, so the two letters are set down for all to see

explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation AI sits openly in L-AI-D, as if exposed; the phrase means revealed or explained.
explanation.definitionFit: To expose something fully is to make it plain, so revealed matches explained.

clue.text: Singer from Bristol having a frolic

parts.note: Bristols is rhyming slang (Bristol Cities) for breasts, so one Bristol is a tit
a lark is a bit of fun, a frolic

explanation.surface: A musician from Bristol enjoys a bit of fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from Bristol' is a trap: Bristol is not a place here but rhyming slang, Bristol City for titty.
explanation.definitionFit: The titlark is a pipit, a songbird, so it is literally a bird that sings.

clue.text: Fisher King getting point of view over

indicators.note: over means in this down clue the perspective word sits above the king's letter

parts.note: an angle is a perspective on something
R is from Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: The Fisher King, of Arthurian legend, comes round to a viewpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler is one who fishes with rod and line.

clue.text: Poser giving pride of place to German kitchen feature

indicators.note: giving pride of place to means the puzzle word lets the German letter go first

parts.note: a poser is a puzzle, a riddle

explanation.surface: A puzzle in which German pride decides where the kitchen gadget goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A griddle is a flat iron plate for cooking, found in kitchens.

clue.text: Ravel pirated timeless rag from one of Gershwin's early movements

definitions.text: rag from one of Gershwin's early movements

indicators.note: to ravel is to tangle, so the letters are tangled into a new order
timeless removes T, the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Ravel steals a rag tune from an early movement of Gershwin's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' drops T from PIRATED, and 'Ravel' rearranges PIRAED. The definition jokes that Gershwin, an American, wore a nappy for his baby's early bowel movements.
explanation.definitionFit: Diaper is the American word for a baby's nappy, a cloth used during infancy.

clue.text: Coat with unusual design on sports girl of a certain shape

indicators.note: with unusual design means the letters of coat are rearranged
sports means wears, so the girl word wraps round the other letters

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A garment with an odd pattern on a sporty girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with unusual design' rearranges coat; 'sports' means wears, so the girl wraps the little word on. 'sports girl' looks like one phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Octagonal describes the eight-sided shape, one particular geometric form.

clue.text: African boss making billions with an American

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for billion

explanation.surface: A boss in Africa earns billions alongside a US partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Bwana is a Swahili word for master or boss used in East Africa.

clue.text: To hell with study, being dulled by too much booze?

parts.note: sod it is a British curse, so sod means to hell with
a den is a private room for working, a study

explanation.surface: A student says forget studying, and gets drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: SOD is a mild British swear word, as in 'sod that'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodden can mean stupefied with drink, as well as soaked through.

clue.text: One actress in Frenzy is most frightening

indicators.note: in Frenzy means the letters are thrown into wild disorder

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: One actress in Hitchcock's film Frenzy is the most terrifying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Frenzy' rearranges I + ACTRESS; Frenzy is also a Hitchcock thriller.
explanation.definitionFit: Scariest is the superlative of scary, meaning causing the greatest fear.
